items.prompt: LQR computes a feedback law u = −Kx that minimizes…
choices: the L1 norm of the state
a quadratic cost on states and inputs over time
items.explain: LQR trades state error (Q) against control effort (R) in a quadratic cost.

items.prompt: For infinite-horizon LQR, the optimal gain comes from solving…
items.explain: The cost-to-go is xᵀPx, where P solves the algebraic Riccati equation; then K = R⁻¹BᵀP.

items.prompt: The separation principle in LQG says you can…
choices: design the Kalman estimator and the LQR controller independently, then combine them
only control systems whose full state is measured
items.explain: For linear-Gaussian problems the optimal output-feedback controller is LQR applied to the Kalman estimate.

items.prompt: The system ẋ = Ax + Bu with n states is controllable iff [B, AB, …, Aⁿ⁻¹B] has…
items.explain: Full rank means the inputs can push the state in every direction of the state space.

items.prompt: By duality, (A, C) is observable iff…
items.explain: The observability matrix of (A, C) is the transpose of the controllability matrix of (Aᵀ, Cᵀ).

items.prompt: Convolution in time corresponds to what in the frequency domain?
items.explain: The convolution theorem: the Fourier transform turns convolution into multiplication.

items.prompt: Why are complex exponentials e^(iωt) eigenfunctions of linear time-invariant systems?
choices: Shifting e^(iωt) only multiplies it by a phase, so the system scales it by its frequency response
items.explain: Time-invariance plus linearity means the output is the input times a complex number H(ω).

items.prompt: Vanilla RNNs struggle with long-range dependencies largely because…
choices: gradients through many time steps vanish or explode
they need labels at every step
items.explain: Backpropagating through time multiplies many Jacobians, whose product shrinks or blows up.

items.prompt: A time-invariant state-space layer such as S4 trains efficiently because it can be computed as…
choices: a long convolution in parallel, and as a recurrence at inference
items.explain: Unrolling an LTI recurrence gives a convolution kernel, which can be applied with FFTs during training.

items.prompt: Why are SSM state matrices parameterized with eigenvalues of negative real part?
choices: To keep the recurrence stable so states do not blow up over long sequences
items.explain: Stable eigenvalues make the impulse response decay, so long sequences stay numerically well behaved.

items.prompt: What makes Mamba's SSM 'selective' compared with S4?
choices: Its state-space parameters depend on the input, so it is no longer time-invariant
items.explain: Input-dependent step sizes and projections let it choose what to remember, at the cost of the convolution view.

items.prompt: Scaled dot-product attention computes weights as…
items.explain: Queries are compared to keys by dot products, scaled by √d, then normalized with a softmax.

items.prompt: Standard self-attention costs O(L²) in sequence length L because…
choices: every query is compared with every key
items.explain: The L×L score matrix is the bottleneck that linear attention and SSMs try to avoid.

items.prompt: A diffusion model generates data by…
choices: learning to reverse a gradual noising process
items.explain: Training teaches a network to denoise; sampling runs the denoiser from pure noise back to data.

items.prompt: The probability-flow ODE of a score-based model is useful because…
choices: it removes the need for a score network
it only works for discrete data
it is a deterministic map with the same marginals as the SDE, enabling exact likelihoods
it always samples in one step
items.explain: Song et al. show the ODE shares marginals with the SDE, so change-of-variables gives likelihoods.

items.prompt: A neural ODE defines dh/dt = f(h, t; θ). What replaces the network's depth?
choices: Integration time, handled by an ODE solver
items.explain: The hidden state evolves continuously; the solver decides how many evaluations to take.

items.prompt: Flow matching trains a model to regress…
choices: a velocity field that carries noise to data along chosen probability paths
items.explain: It is simulation-free: the target velocity along each path is known in closed form.

items.prompt: In reinforcement learning, a policy maps…
items.explain: The policy is the decision rule; value functions and models support choosing it.

items.prompt: A Lyapunov function for an equilibrium is positive definite and…
items.explain: A decreasing energy-like function certifies stability without solving the dynamics.

items.prompt: Backpropagation computes gradients using…
choices: the chain rule applied backward through the computation graph
items.explain: Reverse-mode differentiation reuses intermediate results, so the gradient costs about one extra pass.
